summary: William Douglas Penneck Hill was an Indologist who studied as a Scholar at King's College, Cambridge (c. 1903–1907). He served as Assistant Master at Eton College and as Principal of Jay Narayan Inter College.

An Indologist and linguist, Whitney studied at Williams College, Yale under Salisbury, and in Germany under Weber, von Roth, and Lepsius. He spent his career at Yale (1853–1894) and served as President of the American Oriental Society (1884–1890).

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Edelglass has taught philosophy at Colby College (attested 2007) and served as a Professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013) and as a Visiting Professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

A scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies educated at the University of London, Soothill served as Director of Shanxi University (1907–1911), worked at National Central University (1911), and was Professor of Chinese at Oxford (1920–1935).

Erskine was an Indologist, historian, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the Royal High School and University of Edinburgh (c. 1787–1792). He founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and served the Literary Society of Bombay (c. 1804–1823).
William Evans Hoyle studied at Owens College from around 1872 to 1874 and subsequently at Christ Church, Oxford, from around 1874 to 1877.

Powell is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Attested at the University of California, Santa Barbara from 1986, he is attested there in 2026 as Emeritus Professor of Religious Studies and Research Professor.

Warren worked in religious studies and philosophy after studying at Wesleyan, Mystical Seven, and Andover Theological Seminary. He taught at the Methodist Episcopal Missionary Institute (1860–1866) and was Boston University's first President and Professor (1873–1911).

An Indologist and historian educated at the University of London, Foster worked at the India Office from 1882 to 1927, serving as Registrar and Superintendent of Records (1907–1927). He was also President of the Hakluyt Society (1928–1945).

Albright worked in history, archaeology, linguistics, and religious studies after studying at Upper Iowa University and Johns Hopkins. He was Acting Director of the American Schools of Oriental Research (1921–1922) and Professor of Semitic Languages at Johns Hopkins (1929–1958).
William Francklin was an Indologist and historian who studied at Westminster School from around 1777 to 1781 and then at Trinity College, Cambridge, from around 1781 to 1782.

Sinclair was an Indologist and historian educated at the Royal School, Armagh. He joined the Indian Civil Service in 1866 and served in administrative positions within the Bombay Presidency from approximately 1869 to 1897.

William Frederick Travers O'Connor was a Tibetologist who studied at Charterhouse School (1884–1887) and the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (c. 1888–1890). He received a post in the Royal Artillery in 1890.
Webster was an Indologist who studied at the City of London School, at Trinity College, Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell (1874), and at Lincoln's Inn (1879).

Archer was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Cambridge (c. 1928–1930) and SOAS University of London (c. 1930–1931). From 1949 to 1959, he served as Keeper of the Indian Section at the Victoria and Albert Museum.
Grey was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who completed an honorary M.A. at the University of Cambridge by 1931. He served as Lecturer in Urdu at Gonville and Caius College from 1929 to 1940.

Sinologist Nienhauser studied at Indiana University under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Bischoff, as well as at Cleveland State, DLI, and Bonn. In 1979 he founded CLEAR, and became Halls-Bascom Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1995.

Indologist William H. Wiser studied at the University of Chicago and Cornell University (Ph.D. c. 1930–1933). He held posts at Sam Higginbottom University (1915) and served as Professor of Rural Sociology at North India Theological College (1933–1941).

Gilbert was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago by 1935. He taught sociology at Auburn University from 1936 to 1937 and held a post at the Library of Congress around 1941.

Moreland was a historian and Indologist educated at Clifton College (1881–1886) and Trinity College, Cambridge (c. 1886–1889). Following his studies, he served in the Indian Civil Service from approximately 1889 to 1914.
